Hon'ble Mayank Kumar Jain,J.

1. Heard learned counsel for the appellant, S.K. Ojha, learned AGA for the State and perused the material placed on record.
2.

The present criminal appeal under Section 14-A(2) Scheduled Castes & Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act has been filed by the appellant to set aside the impugned order dated 12.10.2023, whereby the Special Judge, SC/ST Act/Additional Sessions Judge, Rampur has rejected the bail application of the appellant moved by him in Case Crime No. 64 of 2023, under Sections 307, 506, 364, 376, 511 IPC and Section 3(1)Da, 3(2)V SC/ST Act, Police Station Milak Khanam,
District Rampur.

sentences.text: 3. The case of the prosecution as per the FIR is that on 16/17.07.2023 at around 01.00 am the informant was heading towards her house with her mother-in-law Nirmala.
The driver and the helper of Truck No.U.P.70 GT 3111 stopped the informant and committed indecent activities.
They threatened the mother-in-law of the informant to life by putting an screw driver on her neck and forcibly kidnapped the informant.

They attempted to commit indecent activities inside the cabin Mukrram vs State Of U.P. And Another on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45949912/
1 with the informant and also attempted to strangulate her.

entities.text: Mukrram vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The mother-in-law of the informant informed about this incident to Rajkumar, the husband of informant.
When Raj Kumar along with Habib Ahmad and Jitendra tried to stop the truck at Dilari, the appellant attempted to crush these persons under the truck with intention to cause their death.
When these two persons tried to flee away from the place of occurrence they were apprehended and were brought to the police station concerned.
FIR was lodged against the appellant and other persons.
4. Learned counsel for the appellants has submitted that appellant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in this case.
No offence is made out against the appellant.
The victim refused to undergo for her medical examination therefore, no offence under Sections 376, 511 of IPC is made out against the appellant.
Since the injuries noted on the person of the informant were found to be simple in nature, therefore, no offence under Section 307 of IPC is made out.
There was a dispute of money with the husband of the informant, therefore, the appellant is implicated in this false incident.
There is no direct or indirect evidence available on record regarding the attempt to murder against the appellant.
No motive has been assigned to appellant to commit the crime.
No offence under SC/ST Act is made out against the appellant.
There are material contradictions in the statements of witnesses.
It is a case of malicious prosecution under the provisions of S.C./S.T. Act.
Appellant is languishing in jail since 17.07.2023 having no criminal history.
In case, the appellant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.

5. Per contra, learned A.G.A. has supported the order passed by the Sessions court and vehemently opposed the prayer for grant of bail to the appellant and argued that the averments made in the FIR itself demonstrate the nature of the offence committed by the appellant.
He along with other co-accused abducted the informant and tried to molest her and attempted to commit murder by strangulating her.
The appellant was apprehended by the husband and other witnesses and was handed over to the police, therefore, the presence of the appellant is certified.
Screw driver is also recovered at the time of arrest of the appellant and other co-accused.

The victim during her statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. has corroborated the version of the prosecution and has specifically stated that she informed the appellant that she belong to SC/ST community appellant addressed her with caste related abuses.
Appellant attempted to commit rape with her by touching her inappropriately.
Independent witnesses Nirmala Devi, Jitendra Kumar, Habib Ahmad and Raj Kumar have corroborated the version of the FIR.
During her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C.
the victim/informant consistently corroborated the version of the prosecution.
There is no contradiction in the statement of witnesses and the version of the prosecution.
6. It appears from the arguments advanced by the counsel for the parties and from perusal of material on record that the trial court has properly considered the case of the appellant.
Hence, in view of above consideration, the order of rejection of bail passed by the trial court dated 12.10.2023 is affirmed.

7. Having considered the submissions of the parties noted above, finding no force in the submissions made by the learned counsel for the appellant; without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the opinion that the appellant is not entitled to be enlarged on bail and the appeal deserves to be dismissed.

sentences.text: 8. The criminal appeal is dismissed.
9. The trial court may make all possible efforts/endeavour and try to conclude the trial expeditiously in accordance with law, if there is no other legal impediment.

10. It is made clear that the observations made in this order are limited to the purpose of determination of this bail application and will in no way be construed as an expression on the merits of the case.
The trial court shall be absolutely free to arrive at its independent conclusions on the basis of evidence led unaffected by anything said in this order.
